messages:
Tara (support): FYI — auditor just escalated a request from a customer incident. They want: KMS key use records (key-id: rk-0a1b2c), access logs for the timeframe 2026-02-14 -> 2026-02-21, and a short repro of the billing/api error that triggered the ticket. 
Devon K.: Got it. Is this the same incident where a spike in 429s correlated with a config rollback? Need the exact API hashes and sample request IDs. 
Tara (support): Yes — ticket #C-91234. They saw rate-limit errors then some billing discrepancies. Auditor wants chain-of-custody for logs and confirmation of retention policy before we hand anything off. 
Maria S.: On KMS: we keep key-usage records in CloudTrail (enabled) and we push consolidated logs to s3://redwood-compliance/kms-usage/YYYY/MM/DD/. For the requested window the files are: s3://redwood-compliance/kms-usage/2026/02/14/part-0001.gz -> part-0006.gz. Files contain eventName: Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataKey, ReEncrypt. 
Kyle (compliance): Important: we must redact user identifiers before sending external copies. Auditor can get a hashed identifier mapping if they need correlation. Also confirm our retention is 3 years for KMS events per policy. 
Tara (support): Auditor asked for sampling on access logs — want assurance we didn't drop logs during the spike window. How do we prove no sampling gaps? 
Maria S.: We have sequence numbers in the log roll metadata and we run a daily completeness check. I can provide the completeness report for Feb 14-21. It includes checksums and sequence ranges. Here's a compressed export (internal link): https://internal.redwood/corp/evidence/exports/C-91234/kms-usage-20260214-20260221.tar.gz 
AuditBot: Evidence package created by automation: export_id=exp-78321a, sha256=3b7f9e2a..., expiry=2026-04-07T23:59:00Z. 
Devon K.: For repro steps on the 429/billing issue — I can capture the minimal reproduction I used in staging. Steps summary: 

```
1) Configure client with concurrency=200 and batch_size=16
2) Run repeated /v1/generate calls with prompt size ~1024 tokens
3) Simulate network retries (5s backoff) for 15 minutes
4) Observe token accounting mismatch in billing job that consumed partial responses
``` 

Devon K.: I'll attach sample request IDs (redacted) from staging and prod where available. 
Kyle (compliance): Timeline note for the auditor: we began preserving a forensic snapshot on 2026-02-23 09:12 UTC immediately after the ticket escalation. That snapshot is immutable and stored in the compliance bucket with access logging enabled. 
Tara (support): Auditor wants explicit statement about inability to export HSM key material — they asked if raw private key bytes exist anywhere. Need a short blurb we can send. 
Maria S.: Short answer: private key material never leaves the HSM; exports are disabled. We can provide the HSM policy dump and the KMS key metadata (key state, origin: HSM, isExportable: false). Example metadata snippet: `{"KeyId":"rk-0a1b2c","Origin":"HSM","KeyState":"Enabled","KeyUsage":"ENCRYPT_DECRYPT","IsExportable":false}` 
Kyle (compliance): Also include the key rotation history CSV and the KMS CMK lifecycle audit (rotation timestamps, admin principal hashes). I will prepare that and redact admin emails. 
Tara (support): Auditor also asked for sampling rationale for access logs vs. full export — they want to know why we sampled and what % of events were included. 
Maria S.: We did not sample KMS events for that window; we shipped full CloudTrail records. For higher-volume API traces we do sampling at 1% by default; the billing route is always logged at 100% and we have the policy enforcement record. I can attach the sampling config file and the relevant rule: `sampling: { route: "/billing/*", rate: 1.0 }` 
Devon K.: ETA for artifacts: completeness report + KMS metadata + repro package by EOD tomorrow (2026-03-24 17:00 PT). I will also add a small script to reproduce the billing mismatch in a container and upload the container image tag. 
AuditBot: ACL check passed for share: recipients allowed = [redwood-audit-team, auditor-jane@auditorfirm]. Download link will expire per policy. 
Kyle (compliance): Action items: (1) Maria upload the completeness checks & metadata to the evidence bundle; (2) Devon upload repro package + sample IDs; (3) Tara draft the external-facing statement about HSM export and retention timeline. I'll review redactions and sign off. 
Tara (support): I'll draft the HSM statement now and post a first-pass here for quick review. 
Maria S.: Uploaded: s3://redwood-compliance/exports/C-91234/completeness-report-20260214-20260221.csv and s3://redwood-compliance/exports/C-91234/kms-metadata.json.gz. Shared links (internal) sent to compliance reviewers. 
Devon K.: Uploaded repro tarball to internal registry: ghcr.io/redwood/repro/C-91234:20260323 and added sample request id list (redacted) to the evidence folder. 
Kyle (compliance): I'll produce the external package and record the chain-of-custody log here once I've completed redactions. Targeting review by 2026-03-25 10:00 PT. 
Tara (support): @Kyle thanks — once you post the final package I'll send it to the auditor and log the disclosure in the compliance tracker. 
AuditBot: Disclosure logged: disclosure_id=dis-99821, timestamp=2026-03-23T22:13:05Z, package=exp-78321a. 
Tara (support): Closing note for thread: if the auditor requests additional raw network captures we'll need SRE approval. For now we have enough artifacts to satisfy the SOC2 evidence request. :white_check_mark:
